messages:
sre-oncall: noticed a spike in apiserver request latency and controller-manager churn in eu3 after schedulers preempted several GPU nodes at 03:14 UTC. etcd leader experienced a brief election.
yvonne: pulling logs now. any network alerts?
diego: no SNAT or conntrack alarms this time. I see repeated kubelet disconnects and nvme write stalls on the host where etcd leader landed. sample: 
```
W0318 03:14:22.987 etcdserver: store backend fsync took 420ms
```
sre-oncall: that aligns with apiserver accept queue lag. controller-manager lost leader lease twice.
yvonne: which node was leader? infra-bot: etcd_leader eu3 = eu3-c-05 (confirmed).
diego: eu3-c-05 had a GPU preemption event while reclaiming resources; the local nvme sustained GC and IO spikes as pods were evicted and images cleaned. volume iops jumped at the same timestamp.
sre-oncall: hypothesis: aggressive GPU preemptions caused heavy disk churn on the leader node -> etcd commit fsync latency -> leader renew jitter -> apiserver and controller-manager experienced errors.
yvonne: mitigation steps: 1) throttle GPU preemptions (set lower preemption-rate for eu3), 2) move etcd leader off the noisy host (mark unsched for leader), 3) add IO pressure alert for control-plane nodes.
diego: cordoning eu3-c-05 for control-plane, requesting graceful leader transfer.
infra-bot: cordon applied. leader moved to eu3-a-02 ; commit latency down to ~22ms.
sre-oncall: apiserver latency recovering, controller-manager stable. monitor for 1h.
yvonne: follow-ups: add preemption cooldown for GPU pools, prefer leader placement on NVMe-light hosts, and add a preempt-probe metric to Redwood Optimize to surface workloads that cause node disk churn.
diego: will add runbook steps to avoid scheduling etcd leaders on hosts with heavy local IO in future.
sre-oncall: logging incident and tagging ENG-PLATFORM and ENG-ML to discuss cost/safety tradeoffs for preemptible GPUs. closing when stable. :thumbsup:
